rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a useful performance baseline. This experiment tests the minimal RNA-only configuration with PCA and a single profile, clarifying how much signal RNA alone contributes. It is the best first use of budget because it is low-cost, minimally confounded, and establishes a reference for later comparisons of RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image-only models, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline, so there is no evidence yet about whether image features are informative. config_010 tests image-only single-profile ResNet50 as the minimal modality comparison, isolating the effect of using image data while avoiding multiprofile aggregation and fusion complexity. This is the best next experiment because it reduces a major uncertainty about modality before investing budget in more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet, so the RNA baseline is the most promising direction. The main uncertainty is whether using multiple profiles with simple aggregation improves performance over the single-profile PCA setup. config_002 tests this directly while keeping the RNA encoder fixed, making it a clean extension that clarifies whether profile aggregation matters before investing in transformer aggregation, stronger RNA encoders, or multimodal fusion.

The best result so far is config_002 (0.5907 acc, 0.5727 F1), showing that multiprofile PCA RNA with avgpool improves over singleprofile PCA RNA (0.4849 acc), but the gain is confounded by profile and aggregation. config_003 keeps model, profile, and RNA encoder fixed and changes only aggregation to transformer, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current promising direction, isolates an important aggregation decision, and avoids changing modality, encoder, or fusion before those effects are better understood.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the strongest setting so far (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), clearly better than singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether this multiprofile avgpool benefit is specific to PCA or also holds for learned RNA representations. config_005 tests scvi_n200 in the same multiprofile avgpool setting, changing only the RNA encoder relative to config_002. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction, isolates the representation effect, and will guide whether to invest further in learned RNA encoders or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation outperform single-profile and transformer-aggregated settings, and scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder tested (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1). However, scgpt is untested under this otherwise best-known setting. config_008 tests scgpt while holding profile setting and aggregation fixed, isolating the effect of RNA representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising profile/aggregation direction while efficiently reducing uncertainty about whether a different RNA encoder can improve validation performance, without introducing confounding image or fusion changes.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool (config_005, 0.650 acc / 0.628 F1), while image-only ResNet50 is weak (config_010, 0.208 acc). The key uncertainty is whether adding image features to the best RNA representation can improve validation accuracy, and whether a simple concat fusion is sufficient. config_030 keeps the best RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed, then adds ResNet50 image features with concat fusion, making it a direct extension of config_005. This is the best next use of budget because it tests the central multimodal question with minimal additional complexity and will clarify whether further investment in image encoders or more complex fusion is justified.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool, which achieved the best validation accuracy and F1 so far. For PCA, avgpool also outperformed transformer, but the aggregation effect for scvi is still untested. config_006 keeps the best RNA encoder and multiprofile setting fixed while testing transformer aggregation, isolating one important design choice. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction, may improve the current best model, and reduces uncertainty about aggregation before spending budget on more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200, where transformer aggregation is best (config_006: 0.653 accuracy / 0.628 F1) and avgpool is close (config_005: 0.650 / 0.628). The only multimodal test so far, config_030 (scvi_n200 + resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, concat), underperformed RNA-only (0.632 / 0.607), leaving uncertainty about whether image can help or whether avgpool/concat was limiting. config_032 keeps the same RNA encoder, profile setting, image encoder, and fusion as config_030 but changes aggregation to transformer, directly testing whether transformer aggregation improves the multimodal model and whether adding image to the best RNA-only transformer setup can beat config_006. This is a controlled exploitation of the most promising RNA direction and a high-value next step before adding further fusion or image-encoder complexity.

The strongest completed result is config_032, a multimodal multiprofile model using scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion, which outperforms the corresponding RNA-only transformer setting and the avgpool multimodal setting. Fusion is still underexplored because only concat has been tested in the best multimodal setup. config_033 changes only the fusion method from concat to weighted, directly testing whether learned modality weighting improves over fixed concatenation while holding the promising RNA encoder, profile setting, image encoder, and aggregation fixed. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal, high-prior extension of the current best configuration and efficiently reduces uncertainty about an important multimodal design choice before introducing larger changes such as a new image encoder.
